title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

Markets remain in pullback mode. The large cap indices are relatively the strongest, holding above rising 10/20/50-day MAs. The IWM is consolidating near the 10/20-day and the MDY tested the 50-day before bouncing back into resistance. With the government shutdown dysfunction weighing on the markets this morning, we’ll have to see how things unfold in the coming sessions. Similar pullbacks have played out in recent weeks, but the key is whether buyers step up again to drive higher momentum from these levels.

Internals are weak with new lows are outpacing new highs, and downside momentum is broadening. With breadth rolling over, the coming week will be pivotal in determining whether this deterioration deepens into a larger pullback or stabilizes.

Sector leadership remains uneven. Strength is concentrated in Technology, Materials, Healthcare, and Consumer, which are driving relative performance. Meanwhile, Defensives, Energy, and Financials continue to lag. This persistent rotation highlights the importance of aligning with sectors showing sustained strength while avoiding groups stuck in structural weakness.

Overall Trend: Mixed

Plan of Action

1. Trend Alignment

  • Major indices are still above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day MAs, but the tone has weakened.

  • The MDY broke below its 3-week range and tested the 50-day before bouncing—treat this as a cautionary signal.

  • If two or more indices break their 20-day MAs on volume, prepare for a more defensive shift.

  • Watch how indices behave on retests of support—resilient buying would be constructive, while failure would reinforce caution.

2. Breadth & Momentum

  • Internals are negative: new lows are outpacing new highs 2-to-1, and downside momentum is dominant.

  • Expect higher breakout failure rates until breadth re-expands.

  • Use breadth/momentum trends as your primary filter for exposure. Do not scale in aggressively until internals show improvement.

3. Sector Allocation

  • Current leaders: Technology, Materials, Utilities, Energy, Consumer.

  • Avoid laggards: Defensives, Industrials, Real Estate.

  • Allocate selectively toward leaders showing tight bases or orderly pullbacks; avoid speculation in sectors under pressure.

  • Keep allocations diversified across leadership groups rather than concentrated in one area.

4. Stock Selection & Setups

  • Apply the breakout framework cautiously:

    • Focus on tight consolidations or orderly pullbacks into rising 10/20-day MAs.

    • Avoid extended or sloppy patterns—false starts are more common in this tape.

    • Only trade names from sectors aligned with leadership.

  • Be prepared to exit quickly if setups stall—don’t let small losses grow in a weakening backdrop.

  • Don’t die from a “death of 1,000 cuts” - meaning you keep trying to overtrade in a weak tape. If you’re getting cut up and breakouts aren’t following through, that doesn’t mean that breakouts stopped working forever - it just means they aren’t working right now. Be patient and let your results guide you.

5. Risk Management & Position Sizing

  • Keep sizing light (½ to ¾ normal) until breadth confirms a healthier backdrop.

  • Place stops at swing lows or below 20-day MAs, keeping them within ATR/ADR limits.

  • Lock partial profits early (⅓–½ after 3–5 days or a 2-3R move).

  • Maintain a 30–40% cash buffer for defense and flexibility.

6. Scenario Triggers

  • Bullish: Breadth expands, new highs outpace new lows, and indices hold above support with follow-through → cautiously add exposure.

  • Neutral: Indices hold support, but breadth/momentum remain negative → maintain selective exposure, keep cash high.

  • Bearish: Indices break 20-day or 50-day MAs on volume, breadth worsens further → cut exposure aggressively, raise cash toward 50%+, consider tactical hedges.

Bottom Line:
The market remains in pullback mode with weakening internals, making long-side follow-through harder to achieve. Stay defensive, trade smaller, and align only with the strongest sectors and setups. Preserve capital until breadth improves and indices prove resilience at support.
